title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Morning Brief – 7 November 2026
headline: Corruption Scrutiny Intensifies in Tamil Nadu as DVAC Books Duraimurugan Over Rs 1,427-Crore Sand Mining Scam

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape faces severe turbulence as high-profile anti-corruption investigations and fierce ideological rows dominate state affairs. The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a landmark corruption case against senior DMK general secretary and former minister Duraimurugan alongside 26 others, alleging a massive loss of Rs 1,427 crore through illegal river sand mining operations between 2021 and 2024. This administrative bombshell coincides with an escalating political firestorm over the Periyar Arivulagam library in Coimbatore, where allegations by noted writer Perumal Murugan regarding substandard, overpriced, and suspected AI-generated books have triggered sharp verbal duels between Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's TVK administration and the opposition DMK.

Simultaneously, the judiciary and state governance structures are grappling with profound institutional shifts. The ruling TVK government has formally disbanded the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations—originally established by the previous DMK regime to champion state autonomy—and transferred its mandate directly to the State Law Commission. Meanwhile, high-stakes political friction continues to play out across the state, marked by contentious arrests in Madurai over alleged MLA horse-trading, extended remands for former DMK ministers facing graft charges, and ongoing legal battles in the Madras High Court and Supreme Court concerning tight assembly election margins and statutory compliance.

sections.government_and_administration: - **TN Government Disbands High-Level Committee on Centre-State Relations, Transmits Mandate to Law Commission:** In a major administrative restructuring issued via a Government Order on November 6, 2026, the Tamil Nadu government officially disbanded the High-Level Committee on Union-State Relations originally constituted during the previous DMK regime in April 2025. The three-member panel, tasked with reviewing constitutional statutes and recommending structural measures to strengthen federalism and state autonomy, has had its entire mandate transferred directly to the State Law Commission. Concurrently, administrative focus remained riveted on urban infrastructure as Transport and Infrastructure Minister Aadhav Arjuna addressed a gathering at Kalaiwanar Arena in Chennai, boldly asserting that the administration's ongoing public transport and roadway overhauls will soon transform local bus corridors into infrastructure matching national highway standards. The administration also addressed civic security following a sensitive incident in Neelankarai where Chennai police successfully counselled a former flight attendant who abandoned her newborn near Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's residence, ensuring the infant received stable medical care under Child Welfare Committee oversight. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/tn-govt-disbands-high-level-committee-on-union-state-relations/article71675771.ece))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **AIADMK Functionary Arrested Over Alleged TVK MLA Poaching Attempt; Judge Releases Accused on Bond:** Special anti-corruption court judge (in-charge) S. Joseph Joy on Friday refused to grant judicial remand to AIADMK functionary and former Madurai deputy mayor P.M. Mannan, releasing him instead on a personal bond of Rs 25,000. Mannan had been arrested by the Central Crime Branch police following a formal complaint filed by TVK’s Madurai Central MLA Madar Badhurudeen, who alleged that the AIADMK leader attempted to offer cash bribes to induce a floor-crossing vote against the ruling government during a no-confidence motion. The presiding judge sharply questioned the rationale of the police action, noting that officers had arbitrarily arrested Mannan on Friday despite having formally issued him a legal summons to appear for police questioning the following day. Political tensions also escalated around former school education minister and DMK leader Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, whose judicial custody in an ongoing private school bribery case was extended by a special Chennai court through November 18, 2026. Meanwhile, DMK MP P. Wilson aggressively championed social justice platforms by publicly welcoming the Supreme Court's definitive ruling on the OBC creamy layer, emphasizing that parental salary limits cannot serve as the sole exclusionary criterion for educational and employment reservations. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/aiadmk-functionary-mannan-held-judge-refuses-custody-releases-him))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Supreme Court Admits DMK Plea Over Narrow Election Defeat While Madras High Court Dismisses Plea on Campaign Violations:** The legal battleground surrounding the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections witnessed significant judicial movement as a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh formally admitted an appeal filed by senior DMK leader K.R. Periyakaruppan. The petition challenges a Madras High Court order that had earlier rejected his election challenge against TVK candidate R. Seenivasa Sethupathi, who secured victory in the April elections by a razor-thin margin of just one vote. The apex court directed all respondents, including Sethupathi, to file their formal counter-affidavits within a strict six-week window. In a parallel proceeding at the Madras High Court, Justice K. Kumaresh Babu dismissed an interlocutory petition filed by ruling TVK MLA Vijayakumar Navalpattu S. Viji, who had sought to throw out an election petition filed by former minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi challenging the Thiruverumbur constituency result. The High Court ruled that substantial factual allegations, including the illegal deployment of children during campaign trails in direct violation of Election Commission guidelines, warrant a comprehensive judicial trial rather than premature dismissal. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/sc-agrees-to-hear-dmk-leaders-plea-challenging-rejection-of-election-petition))
sections.district_developments: - **Coimbatore and Madurai Witness Intensified Political Fallout Over Library Procurement and Corruption Charges:** District administrations across Coimbatore and Madurai became central focal points for administrative friction and political confrontation following the unfolding Periyar Arivulagam library book procurement scandal and high-profile local arrests. In Coimbatore, local Communist Party of India (Marxist) and Communist Party of India leaders, including state secretaries P. Shanmugam and M. Veerapandian, staged coordinated protests demanding an independent judicial investigation into the massive influx of substandard and overpriced Tamil literature allegedly foisted upon the public library. Local academic and literary circles in Coimbatore expressed deep outrage over the intellectual fraud, prompting district educational authorities to secure the facility and launch internal verification audits. Simultaneously, in Madurai, the arrest and immediate judicial release of former deputy mayor P.M. Mannan by the Central Crime Branch sent shockwaves through local AIADMK cadres, triggering localized protests and heavy police deployments outside police headquarters to manage rival political demonstrations over the alleged MLA horse-trading conspiracy. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/intellectual-fraud-questions-librarys-credibility-left))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Over the next 24 to 48 hours, political observers and state policymakers will closely monitor developments surrounding the DVAC's sand mining investigation into senior DMK leaders, anticipate potential legal challenges and counter-filings in the Supreme Court regarding the one-vote assembly victory dispute, and track opposition protest dates concerning the Periyar Arivulagam book procurement scandal. Additional scrutiny will center on upcoming legislative committee adjustments following the formal transfer of Centre-State relations mandates to the State Law Commission.
